exposure: antenatal betamethasone (BMZ) latency period (<14 days vs. >14 days prior to delivery)
outcome: early neonatal hypoglycemia (blood glucose <40 mg/dL within 48h of birth)
severe neonatal hypoglycemia (blood glucose <25 mg/dL within 48h of birth)
treatment for neonatal hypoglycemia with dextrose gel or IV dextrose
cohort: The study included 758 maternal-infant dyads from a single institution who received antenatal betamethasone during pregnancy and delivered at >=37 weeks gestational age.
finding: A shorter latency period (<14 days) between antenatal betamethasone administration and delivery was not associated with an increased incidence or treatment of neonatal hypoglycemia in term infants compared to a longer latency period (>14 days).
birth_weight: Median 3.03 kg (recent BMZ group) and 3.29 kg (remote BMZ group)
gest_age: Term infants (>=37 weeks gestational age); median 37.1 weeks (recent BMZ group) and 38.4 weeks (remote BMZ group)
